items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; it only reads the context it is sent, so with only the newest message it cannot resolve "it". Option a shows the misconception that the model remembers earlier calls by itself (M7); option c assumes notes are searched without the program doing it.

Call 1: 900. Call 2: 900 + 60 + 500 = 1,460. Call 3: 1,460 + 60 + 1,000 = 2,520. Total 900 + 1,460 + 2,520 = 4,880. Answering 2,520 counts only the last call, and 2,520 minus nothing summed once counts each text once; the transcript is re-sent in full on each call.
Information must be written to storage outside the model and read back into the next session's context. A larger window or a firmer prompt does not carry anything between sessions (M8 for option b).

items.answer: Only a few chunks are relevant, and everything in the context is paid for on every call and can crowd out attention, so a small relevant set is cheaper and works better.
accepted: it costs fewer tokens and keeps the context focused on what is relevant
the whole manual would be re-sent and paid for on every call and dilute attention
items.rationale: Full credit needs the cost or attention reason. Saying the manual does not fit is partial at best: a large window might hold it, but sending it is still wasteful (M8).

Availability changes hourly, so a saved copy goes stale; it should be fetched from the booking system by a tool each time. The other facts are stable and per-student, so they suit notes (though training status may also be better read from the official record).
